Join an exposure table to counts by place and day

Source: R/apx.R
expjn.Rd

Makes the analysis table of the estimators of this family: the rows of the outcome table (place, day, count, ...) with the exposure of the same place and day joined on. Exposure may come from monitors (assigned to areas beforehand, for example by inverse squared distance from the three nearest, as Bondy, Roth and Sager do) or from crimlab's dispersion functions (gplume(), plmfld()).

Usage

expjn(expo, outc, by = c("area", "day"))

# S3 method for class 'expjn'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'expjn'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

expo

The exposure table: a data frame with the key columns and one or more value columns.

outc

The outcome table: a data frame with the key columns.

by

The names of the key columns, in both tables.

...

Not used.

object, x

An object of class expjn.

Value

An object of class expjn, a list: data, the joined table (the outcome table's columns, then the exposure's other columns); nout, nexp; unout, the keys of the outcome rows left out. summary() returns the counts as a data frame.

Details

Duplicate keys in either table are refused: a place with two exposures on one day has no single value to join. Outcome rows without an exposure are left out of data and counted in nout (their keys in unout); exposure rows without an outcome are counted in nexp. Keys are compared as text, so a day given as a date in one table must be a date in the other.

See also

ppmlfe(), plmfld()

Examples

ex <- data.frame(
  area = c("a", "a", "b"),
  day = c(1, 2, 1),
  pm = c(10, 12, 8)
)
oc <- data.frame(area = c("a", "a", "b", "b"), day = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
                 crimes = c(3, 1, 0, 2))
j <- expjn(ex, oc)
j
#> expjn: 3 rows joined; 1 outcome row(s) without an exposure left out; 0 exposure row(s) without an outcome
j$data
#>   area day crimes pm
#> 1    a   1      3 10
#> 2    a   2      1 12
#> 3    b   1      0  8
